title: restate/1.0 - does a human review survive a Mathlib or anchor bump
$comment: env_digest includes every package revision, so `statement_stable` is not_applicable across environments BY CONSTRUCTION -- a single bump invalidates 100% of human review at once, and recovery costs the entire original review budget, per bump, at ~2h an entry. This artifact is what stands between that and re-reviewing everything. It carries three outcomes and NO aggregate: `not_checkable` is not `changed`, and collapsing them would send a reviewer to re-read a statement that may be perfectly fine while hiding that the tool failed.

counts.$comment: Per outcome, never totalled. A single number here would be the aggregate token every schema in this contract refuses.

outcome.$comment: `restated`: elaborates and is defeq -- the review survives. `changed`: elaborates, not defeq -- the review is invalidated and must be redone. `not_checkable`: could not be parsed or elaborated, so NOBODY KNOWS whether it changed.

reason.$comment: Why. Mandatory in shape for not_checkable -- 'parse failed' and 'elaboration logged an error' send a reviewer to different places, and an outcome nobody can act on is not a finding.

allOf.$comment: A not_checkable with no reason is unactionable.
